IV Concept Acupuncturist IV-A Overview Based on the empirical analysis in § III , we identify the need for a more precise and efficient fine-tuning approach. Our key idea is to leverage SAEs for feature-level localization and intervention, while internalizing their corrections into model parameters through localized fine-tuning. Unlike prior methods that attach SAEs to the final model during inference [ 22 , 23 , 43 ] , we instead use them to construct supervision signals for parameter optimization. This design introduces no additional inference overhead while embedding the unlearning effect directly into model parameters, thereby addressing S1 and supporting S2 , while requiring attackers to perform weight-level manipulation rather than merely bypass inference-time interventions. Meanwhile, we localize the update to a single cross-attention block most relevant to the target concept, thus avoiding end-to-end optimization along the full diffusion trajectory and reducing the computational cost of fine-tuning. An overview of our approach is shown in Figure 3 . We begin with feature localization to identify the block most strongly associated with the target concept, along with its corresponding features. We establish mappings between semantic concepts and cross-attention blocks, and apply the feature localization algorithm introduced in § IV-B to automatically identify both the target block and the corresponding features to be modified. This joint localization substantially narrows the fine-tuning scope, enabling faster and more targeted updates. Subsequently, we construct fine-tuning datasets by modifying the localized features controlled by a scaling factor a a (defined in § IV-C ) and projecting them back to the output space of the corresponding cross-attention block. These corrected representations serve as supervision signals for subsequent parameter optimization. Crucially, instead of performing end-to-end diffusion inference during training, we only need a single forward pass to record input–output pairs of the identified cross-attention block along the denoising trajectory, enabling inference-free fine-tuning. Finally, we perform block fine-tuning using a joint objective (Eq. ( 11 ) in § IV-D ) that balances target concept suppression and preservation of generation quality. The resulting parameter updates internalize the SAE-based feature corrections into the model, enabling precise concept erasure without additional inference-time components. The updated cross-attention block is then used in place of the original block during generation. Overall, this framework enables precise and interpretable unlearning across different concept categories. IV-B Feature Localization As shown in the first panel of Figure 3 , ConceptACP begins with feature localization. To remove a specific concept, we first identify its corresponding features and the cross-attention block in which they are most strongly represented. Prior work [ 33 ] reports that four SAEs trained on cross-attention blocks provide interpretable representations of distinct visual elements. Guided by this observation, we use publicly available general-purpose SAEs as the candidate pool to localize the features and target block associated with the concept, without requiring additional SAE training. Notably, ConceptACP can also utilize task-specific SAEs, although the publicly available SAEs already provide sufficiently informative features for precise localization in our experiments. Although it is possible to identify features related to a given concept by examining the feature heatmaps or manipulating feature activations to observe the resulting changes in generated images, this process is time-consuming and unreliable, particularly when concept-related activations are weak or ambiguous. Moreover, while SAEs promote sparse representations, a given concept may still correspond to multiple features, particularly when training data for that concept is limited or when the concept involves diverse visual elements. As shown in Figure 4 , our preliminary analysis indicates that feature #4913 on down.2.1 can effectively remove Nudity , whereas suppressing any one of the top-5 most activated features individually fails to fully eliminate Church .
